claims.text: The propensity of CrFeCoNiX alloys to maintain a protective oxide above 900 °C is governed by whether Si or Al can generate a high-entropy, single-phase oxide.
The relevant high-entropy oxide is structurally homogeneous and adherent.
A single-phase CrFeCoNiX metallic solid solution has a sufficiently uniform elemental distribution to direct homogeneous oxidation.
Uniform elemental distribution in the metal drives formation of a coherent alumina- or silica-like mixed-metal oxide.
The proposed protective oxide expands minimally and accommodates thermal stresses.
Multiphase CrFeCoNiX alloys contain local compositional heterogeneities that lead to unstable, non-cohesive oxides.
Mn-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys form less stable oxides than corresponding Si- or Al-containing alloys.
Si and Al favor thermodynamically stable, slow-growing oxide compounds in CrFeCoNiX alloys.
High configurational entropy stabilizes a homogeneous, single-phase oxide structure.
A homogeneous entropy-stabilized oxide minimizes lattice mismatch and thermal-expansion mismatch stresses.
Reducing lattice and thermal-expansion mismatch stresses lowers the likelihood of oxide cracking and spallation.
Heterogeneous oxidation kinetics in multiphase or Mn-containing alloys promote phase separation within the oxide and thereby cause mechanical instability and spallation.

Single-phase Si- or Al-containing CrFeCoNiX alloys will retain more stable, coherent, and adherent oxide layers above 900 °C than Mn-containing or multiphase alloys under identical exposure conditions.
A multiphase CrFeCoNiMn baseline will develop unstable, non-coherent oxide scales under the specified oxidative or corrosive conditions.
